Fadeaway World |url=https://fadeawayworld.net/marcus-smart-becomes-first-guard-since-gary-payton-to-win-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year |access-date=2025-12-17 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-21 |title=Marcus Smart Is an Elite Defender—With or Without a DPOY Honor |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/04/21/celtics-marcus-smart-is-elite-defender-with-or-without-dpoy-honor |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodriguez • • |first=Tristi |date=2022-05-30 |title=Kerr explains why Smart is 'the guard version' of Draymond |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/kerr-explains-why-smart-is-the-guard-version-of-draymond/1416895/ |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-11-07 |title=The Celtics' Best Defensive Big Man Is 6-foot-3 |url=https://www.theringer.com/2019/11/07/nba/boston-celtics-marcus-smart-defense-frontcourt |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=www.theringer.com |language=en}}</ref> he has been selected to the [[NBA All-Defensive First Team]] thrice and was the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] in [[2021–22 NBA season#Yearly awards|2022]], becoming only the second point guard after [[Gary Payton]] to win the award. Smart played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]].

Smart was drafted by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the sixth overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft|2014 NBA Draft]]. He initially came off the bench for the Celtics before becoming the starting point guard in 2018. Smart helped the Celtics reach the [[NBA Finals]] in [[2022 NBA Finals|2022]]. After eight seasons in Boston, he was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. However, after greatly struggling with injuries in Memphis, Smart was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2025. In July 2025, he signed a two-year contract with the Lakers as a free agent, following a buyout agreement with the Wizards and subsequent clearance through waivers.

'''Malik JonMikal Beasley'''<ref name="bbref">{{cite web|title=Malik Beasley|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/beaslma01.html|website=Basketball Reference|access-date=December 7, 2023}}</ref> ({{IPAc-en|m|ə|ˈ|l|iː|k}} {{respell|mə|LEEK}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> born November 26, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). He attended [[St. Francis Schools|Saint Francis School]] in Alpharetta, Georgia,<ref name="ajc">{{cite news|first=Ken|last=Sugiura|url=http://www.myajc.com/sports/college/alpharetta-malik-beasley-shines-for-fsu/1qgiyVIBMy1ARy6E50EYMP/|title=Alpharetta's Malik Beasley shines for FSU|work=MyAJC.com|date=February 16, 2016|access-date=February 16, 2016}}</ref> where he was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]].

Beasley had a standout freshman season at Florida State, earning freshman-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) honors<ref name="usatoday">{{cite news|date=March 16, 2016|title=2015-16 all-ACC award teams, individual award winners|work=[[USA Today]]|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2016/03/06/2015-16-all-acc-award-teams-individual-award-winners/81410252/|access-date=December 7, 2023|archive-date=January 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116041448/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2016/03/06/2015-16-all-acc-award-teams-individual-award-winners/81410252/|url-status=live}}</ref> after averaging 15.6 points and 5.3 rebounds per game. He led the team in scoring and helped lead the Seminoles to a 20–14 record and berth in the [[2016 NIT|NIT Tournament]]. Beasley declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]] following this freshman season.

He was drafted by the [[Denver Nuggets]] with the 19th overall pick in the 2016 draft. Beasley saw limited minutes off the bench his first two seasons but took on a larger role in his third year, averaging over 11 points in 81 games played. After three and a half seasons with the Nuggets, Beasley was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in February 2020. He had the highest scoring output of his career in his first season and a half with the Timberwolves, averaging 19.9 points over 51 games. He played for four more NBA teams before being accused of illegal [[sports betting]] in 2025. Federal investigators reportedly dropped the investigation thereafter.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |date=August 22, 2025 |title=Attorneys: Malik Beasley no longer target of gambling probe |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46047941/attorneys-malik-beasley-no-longer-target-gambling-probe |access-date=April 28, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>
